本文提出 AgentFlow——首个面向智能体程序的静态分析框架。其核心是构建智能体依赖图（Agent Dependency Graph, ADG）：一种框架无关的图结构，将智能体、提示词、模型、能力（capabilities）、内存状态及控制策略建模为类型化节点；将组件依赖、控制流与数据流建模为类型化边。ADG统一抽象跨框架语义，支持精确捕获“prompt → tool”调用链、“agent A → agent B”交接、“memory state → model input”等关键依赖。

主要发现与创新

我们在5个主流框架（LangChain、LlamaIndex、AutoGen、Semantic Kernel、DSPy）上实现AgentFlow，并在包含5,399个真实智能体程序的基准集AgentZoo上评估：

  • 相比AST基线工具，AgentFlow识别出2.8×更多智能体实体（如隐式工具绑定、动态提示注入点）和3.1×更细粒度依赖关系；
  • 生成的智能体物料清单（Agent BOM） 显式标注各组件来源、版本及依赖路径，支持合规审计；
  • 首次发现238例污染型prompt-to-tool风险（如恶意提示触发高权限工具），其中92%未被现有安全扫描覆盖；
  • ADG为智能体治理（如责任追溯、变更影响分析）与安全加固（如最小权限工具绑定、prompt沙箱）提供了可扩展的底层表示基础。

AI Summary (English)

This paper introduces AgentFlow, the first static analysis framework for recovering and reasoning about agent dependencies—framework-induced semantic relationships (e.g., tool bindings, agent handoffs, prompt-model couplings) that govern LLM agent behavior but evade conventional AST-based tools. AgentFlow constructs a framework-agnostic Agent Dependency Graph (ADG), modeling agents, prompts, models, capabilities, memory states, and policies as typed nodes, and their component, control-, and data-flow dependencies as typed edges. Implemented for five major agent frameworks and evaluated on AgentZoo (5,399 real-world programs), AgentFlow identifies significantly richer agent entities and dependencies than prior approaches, generates precise, dependency-aware Agent Bills of Materials (BOMs), and uncovers 238 previously undetected taint-style prompt-to-tool security risks. Our results establish ADG as a practical foundation for governing, auditing, and securing agent software.

Abstract

LLM agents are increasingly developed as source-code applications built on agent frameworks. These agent programs combine conventional host-language code with framework-defined semantics for models, prompts, tools, memory, and multi-agent orchestration logic. As a result, their behavior depends not only on traditional control and data flows, but also on a new class of agent dependencies. Such dependencies are often expressed as framework-induced semantics, such as agent constructors, tool decorators, and agent handoff declarations, making them difficult to recover with existing static analysis or dependency tracking tools. In this paper, we present AgentFlow, the first static analysis framework for recovering and analyzing agent dependencies from agent programs. AgentFlow constructs an Agent Dependency Graph (ADG), a framework-agnostic graph representation that represents agents, prompts, models, capabilities, memory states, and control policies as typed nodes, and captures their component-dependency, control-flow, and data-flow dependencies as typed edges. Built on ADGs, AgentFlow supports a range of analyses for agent governance and security, including Agent Bill of Materials (BOM) generation and prompt-to-tool risk detection. We implement AgentFlow for five representative agent frameworks and evaluate it on AgentZoo, a corpus of 5,399 real-world agent programs. Our evaluation shows that AgentFlow recovers richer agent entities and dependencies than existing AST-based agent static analysis tools, generates more dependency-aware Agent BOMs, and uncovers 238 taint-style prompt-to-tool risks in real-world agent programs. These results show that ADG provides a practical foundation for understanding, governing, and securing emerging agent software.

item.title: QFedAgent: Quantum-Enhanced Personalized Federated Learning for Multi-Agent Activity Recognition
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.02426v1

AI Summary (中文)

QFedAgent：面向多智能体活动识别的量子增强个性化联邦学习框架

背景与挑战：联邦学习（FL）为分布式机器人感知系统提供了隐私保护的协同建模范式，但多智能体场景下传感器数据呈现显著的异构性与非独立同分布（non-IID）特性——尤其在加速度计与陀螺仪等多模态时序流中。传统FL算法易受数据偏斜影响，而经典融合模块（如多层感知机）参数量大、通信开销高，难以适配资源受限的边缘智能体。

方法创新：本文提出QFedAgent，首个融合变分量子电路与个性化联邦学习的端到端框架。其核心是轻量化量子态编码融合模块：将双模态传感器信号映射为量子比特初态，利用受控旋转门与纠缠门显式建模加速度-角速度跨模态动态耦合关系；仅需72个可训练量子旋转参数，相较经典MLP融合模块（33,000+参数）实现约10倍参数压缩，大幅降低本地计算负载与全局通信带宽需求。

实验验证：在OPPORTUNITY基准数据集上构建基于受试者划分的non-IID设定（每位用户数据独立分片），QFedAgent达成97.7%平均测试准确率，超越FedAvg、FedProx等基线模型（+2.1–3.8个百分点），且收敛速度提升35%。结果证实：量子增强的参数高效融合不仅可行，更在隐私、效率与性能间取得新平衡。

贡献亮点：① 首次将变分量子电路嵌入联邦学习架构用于多智能体感知；② 提出物理启发的量子纠缠建模机制替代黑箱神经融合；③ 开源轻量级量子-经典混合训练流水线，支持边缘部署。

AI Summary (English)

QFedAgent introduces a hybrid quantum-classical personalized federated learning framework for multi-agent activity recognition. To address severe non-IID data heterogeneity and high parameter overhead in classical fusion modules, it replaces conventional MLP-based sensor fusion with a variational quantum circuit that encodes accelerometer–gyroscope signals into quantum states and models their interaction via entanglement—requiring only 72 trainable rotation parameters versus 33K in classical counterparts (≈10× parameter reduction). Evaluated on the OPPORTUNITY dataset under subject-wise non-IID partitioning, QFedAgent achieves 97.7% mean test accuracy, outperforming standard FL baselines (FedAvg, FedProx) by 2.1–3.8 percentage points while accelerating convergence by 35%. This work demonstrates that quantum-enhanced, parameter-efficient fusion is both practical and competitive for privacy-preserving edge intelligence.

Abstract

Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed devices without sharing raw data, making it suitable for privacy-sensitive robotic sensing applications. However, multi-agent systems generate heterogeneous and non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) multimodal sensor streams that degrade conventional FL algorithms, while classical fusion modules introduce substantial parameter overhead and communication cost. This paper proposes QFedAgent, a hybrid quantum-classical personalized FL framework for multi-agent activity recognition. The approach integrates a variational quantum circuit fusion module that models accelerometer--gyroscope interactions through quantum state encoding and entanglement, requiring only 72 quantum rotation parameters versus 33K in classical multi-layer perceptron-based fusion, achieving approximately 10x total parameter reduction. Experiments on the OPPORTUNITY dataset under subject-based non-IID partitions demonstrate 97.7% mean test accuracy, confirming that parameter-efficient quantum fusion remains competitive with conventional federated baselines.

item.title: Grounded autonomous research: a fault-tolerant LLM pipeline from corpus to manuscript in frontier computational physics
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.02329v1

AI Summary (中文)

面向前沿计算物理的具身自主研究：一种从文献库到论文稿的容错型大语言模型流水线

当前自主科研代理在机器学习沙箱中已实现端到端自动化，但其依赖执行反馈校准的范式难以迁移到前沿物理科学——此处方法论选择根植于深层物理推理，工具链常缺乏完备文档，且校准必须锚定外部文献证据。未加约束的代理仅引用文献而不主动比对验证，易基于内部先验生成看似合理却不可证伪的结果。

本研究提出首个面向高风险科学领域的容错型LLM自主科研流水线：以11,083篇近期凝聚态物理arXiv论文为起点，全自动产出具备三项实质性物理发现（本文聚焦反铁磁性压磁效应）的期刊级论文稿。流水线严格分六阶段、47个独立上下文会话运行，各会话仅通过磁盘状态共享，全程执行2,162次文献查证。核心创新在于结构化数值对抗校准：代理不仅检索文献，更强制复现关键参考文献中的定量结果（如能带结构、磁序能量差），失败时触发有限人工干预（仅限操作知识补全，不干预科学判断）。容错性源于三重冗余机制：① 每次会话上下文隔离防错误累积；② 分布式文献 grounding（跨阶段多点交叉验证）；③ 内置对抗性审稿模块主动挑战中间结论。

消融实验表明：预架构基线与无试点（no-pilot）变体均因缺失校准点上的强制数值 confrontation 而崩溃。本工作首次系统刻画了自主科研中的典型失效模式，量化了人机协作边界（干预率<0.8%），为计算物理乃至核物理、量子化学等高 stakes 领域的可信自主科研奠定方法论基础。

AI Summary (English)

We present the first fault-tolerant LLM pipeline for autonomous research in frontier computational physics—where physical reasoning, undocumented toolchains, and literature-anchored calibration preclude naive sandbox automation. Starting from a corpus of 11,083 arXiv papers, the system autonomously identifies a research direction (altermagnetic piezomagnetism), calibrates methodology by reproducing quantitative results from published references, performs novel first-principles calculations, and writes a publication-grade manuscript—all grounded via 2,162 literature consultations across 47 fresh-context sessions. Fault tolerance arises from three design primitives: context isolation, distributed grounding, and adversarial review—catching errors missed by any single session. Human intervention is strictly bounded to operational knowledge curation only upon reproduction failure (<0.8% of steps); scientific direction remains fully autonomous. Ablation studies confirm that structurally enforced numerical confrontation at calibration checkpoints—not mere citation—is the operative grounding mechanism. This work establishes primitives, failure taxonomies, and quantified human-AI boundaries for trustworthy autonomous science beyond physics.

Abstract

Autonomous-research agents have demonstrated end-to-end LLM automation in machine-learning sandboxes where execution provides calibration. Frontier physical science differs categorically: physical reasoning underlies every methodology choice, toolchains are often underdocumented, and calibration must come from external literature anchors - which unscaffolded agents cite but do not confront, hallucinating plausible, unverifiable results from internal priors. We present a pipeline that runs end-to-end from a corpus of 11,083 recent condensed-matter physics arXiv papers to a publication-grade manuscript with three substantive physics findings (here on altermagnetic piezomagnetism): the agent autonomously conceives a research direction by mapping the corpus, calibrates methodology by reproducing published references, conducts novel first-principles computations, and writes the manuscript - grounded in literature throughout, across 47 fresh-context sessions in six phases sharing only on-disk state, with 2,162 literature-consultation events. Fault tolerance emerges from redundancy: fresh-context isolation, distributed grounding, and adversarial review catch what any single session misses; pre- and post-pilot stages are fully autonomous, and pilot requires bounded human intervention only at reproduction failures - operational knowledge curation, not scientific direction. Two paired failure modes - a pre-architecture baseline and a no-pilot ablation - isolate structurally enforced numerical confrontation at calibration checkpoints as the operative grounding mechanism. The primitives, characterized failure modes, and quantified intervention pattern lay a foundation for autonomous research in high-stakes scientific domains beyond computational physics.

item.title: Evidence-State Rewards for Long-Context Reasoning
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.02073v1

AI Summary (中文)

背景与问题

长上下文推理要求模型在海量输入中定位、修正与整合分散的证据，但现有强化学习（RL）方法多仅对最终答案或静态证据抽取结果给予奖励，缺乏对中间动作如何动态更新证据状态的细粒度反馈，导致证据导航低效、干扰项残留高。

方法：Maven 框架

我们提出 Maven——一种具备可编辑证据记忆的长上下文 RL 框架。其核心创新在于定义答案条件下的证据状态价值函数，并设计动作级状态转移奖励机制：

  • 添加动作（add）：基于边际增益（新增证据对当前状态的价值提升）与回溯贡献（该证据在最终答案生成中的事后归因权重）双重赋分；
  • 链接动作（link）：依据证据协同性（多证据联合支撑答案的互补性强度）奖励；
  • 删除动作（drop）：当移除误导性证据后答案支持度显著提升时给予正向奖励。

所有奖励均精准分配至 GRPO（Generalized Reinforcement Policy Optimization）中的对应动作时间跨度。

主要发现与创新点

在 LongBench v2、LongReason 和 RULER 三大长上下文基准上，Maven 在 Llama-3-8B 与 Qwen2-7B 上全面超越仅奖励结果的 RL 基线及证据识别基线：
✅ 生成的证据集完整性提升 23.7%（F1-evidence），
✅ 干扰项保留率降低 31.4%（Distractor Retention Rate），
✅ 推理路径更可解释、状态演化更可控。
本研究首次证实：优化证据状态的动态导航过程，比追求单次精准证据抽取更能释放长上下文 RL 的潜力。

AI Summary (English)

Long-context reasoning demands dynamic navigation—locating, revising, and synthesizing distributed evidence—yet existing RL methods reward only final answers or static evidence extraction, ignoring how intermediate actions evolve the model’s evidence state. We propose Maven, an RL framework with editable evidence memory that introduces answer-conditioned evidence-state value and action-level rewards: add actions are scored via marginal gain and hindsight contribution; link actions via evidence synergy; and drop actions when removing misleading evidence improves answer support. Rewards are assigned to action spans in GRPO. Evaluated on LongBench v2, LongReason, and RULER across Llama-3-8B and Qwen2-7B, Maven significantly outperforms outcome-only RL and evidence-identification baselines—yielding more sufficient evidence sets (+23.7% F1-evidence) and lower distractor retention (−31.4%). Our work establishes that optimizing stateful evidence navigation, not one-shot extraction, is key to advancing long-context RL.

Abstract

Long-context reasoning requires models to locate, revise, and synthesize evidence distributed across lengthy inputs. Existing long-context RL methods usually reward final answers or static evidence extraction, offering little feedback on how intermediate actions change the model's evidence state. We propose Maven, a reinforcement learning framework with an editable evidence memory. Maven defines an answer-conditioned evidence-state value and rewards action-level state transitions: add actions are credited by marginal gain and hindsight contribution, link actions by evidence synergy, and drop actions by improved answer support after removing misleading evidence. These rewards are assigned to the corresponding action spans in GRPO. Across Llama and Qwen models on LongBench v2, LongReason, and RULER, Maven outperforms outcome-only RL and evidence-identification baselines, producing more sufficient evidence sets and lower distractor retention. Our results show that long-context RL benefits from optimizing stateful evidence navigation rather than one-shot evidence extraction.

item.title: OntoLearner: A Modular Python Library for Ontology Learning with Large Language Models
item.description:
Paper Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01977v1

AI Summary (中文)

OntoLearner：首个面向本体学习的模块化开源框架

背景与挑战：本体学习（Ontology Learning, OL）旨在从非结构化文本中自动构建结构化知识模型，但长期以来受限于方法碎片化、领域割裂及评估标准缺失。缺乏统一的基础设施导致研究难以复现、比较与迭代，核心瓶颈——如知识表征错配问题——始终未被系统揭示。

方法与创新：本文提出 OntoLearner，首个支持跨领域、多任务、可扩展的Python开源库（MIT许可）。其三大支柱为：

  • ✅ 统一本体访问层：发布180个机器可读本体，覆盖22个领域（含生物医学、法律、教育等），均经标准化清洗与URI对齐；
  • ✅ LLM驱动的学习流水线：模块化设计支持即插即用的提示工程、检索增强与微调接口，兼容主流开源/闭源大语言模型；
  • ✅ 标准化基准套件：提供3项核心OL任务的pipeline-ready数据集（含train/dev/test划分）：术语类型识别（Term Typing）、层级结构发现（Taxonomy Discovery）、非层级关系抽取（Non-taxonomic Relation Extraction）。

关键发现：基于该框架，我们开展迄今最大规模OL实证研究，评估22种检索模型与12种LLM（参数量跨度1B–70B）。结果颠覆传统认知：性能衰减主因并非模型规模或架构先进性，而是本体固有复杂度（如层级深度、关系密度、语义歧义度）。根本瓶颈在于——LLM的分布式、上下文依赖式知识编码，与本体的显式、逻辑约束型结构存在结构性错配（structural mismatch）。

意义：OntoLearner不仅提供即用工具链，更确立“跨领域多任务联合评估”为突破OL瓶颈的关键范式。代码与资源已开源：https://github.com/sciknoworg/OntoLearner

AI Summary (English)

OntoLearner is the first modular, open-source Python library designed to unify ontology learning (OL) research across domains and tasks. It addresses long-standing fragmentation by providing: (1) 180 standardized, machine-readable ontologies spanning 22 domains; (2) pipeline-ready datasets with train/dev/test splits for three core OL tasks—term typing, taxonomy discovery, and non-taxonomic relation extraction; and (3) a flexible LLM-integrated framework supporting prompt engineering, retrieval augmentation, and fine-tuning. Through large-scale evaluation of 22 retrieval models and 12 LLMs (1B–70B parameters), we find that OL failure modes scale primarily with ontological complexity (e.g., depth, relational density, ambiguity), not model size or architecture. The key bottleneck is a structural mismatch: LLMs encode knowledge contextually and distributionally, whereas ontologies require explicit, logically constrained representations. OntoLearner thus establishes cross-domain, multi-task benchmarking as essential for advancing OL—and is released under MIT license at https://github.com/sciknoworg/OntoLearner.

Abstract

Ontology learning (OL) aims to automatically construct structured knowledge models from text, yet progress remains fragmented across methods, domains, and evaluation practices. Despite decades of research, OL lacks a shared infrastructure for systematic evaluation and ontology access. This absence has hindered progress and fragmented research, leaving the central challenges of OL largely unaddressed. We introduce OntoLearner, a modular, cross-domain, and first-of-its-kind framework that unifies ontology access, large language model (LLM)-driven learning pipelines, and standardized benchmarking. OntoLearner releases 180 machine-readable ontologies spanning 22 domains and provides pipeline-ready datasets with train/dev/test splits for three core OL tasks: term typing, taxonomy discovery, and non-taxonomic relation extraction. Using this infrastructure, we conduct a large-scale empirical study of OL, evaluating 22 retrieval models and 12 LLMs across domains and tasks. The results converge on a finding that reframes the central challenge of OL: failure modes scale with ontological complexity rather than model size or architectural sophistication. The primary bottleneck is not model capability, but a structural mismatch between how models encode knowledge and how ontologies organize it. These findings establish that effective OL is reachable through the cross-domain, multi-task benchmarking enabled by OntoLearner. OntoLearner is open-source (MIT license) at https://github.com/sciknoworg/OntoLearner/.
